description: Working on a Python-based software application for NASA Space Apps. The focus is on leveraging data processing, Machine Learning (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn), and interactive web dashboards (Streamlit/Dash) to build a functional solution for space metrics analysis and health monitoring.
summary: Long-duration missions expose astronauts to radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a closed environment, and with communication delays they must spot health changes themselves. AstroVitals is a self-monitoring dashboard that compares each astronaut with their own baseline across cardiovascular, bone/muscle, immune and behavioral indicators, plus radiation dose. A machine learning model (Isolation Forest) flags unusual patterns, and plain-language actions tell the astronaut what to do and when to contact the flight surgeon. It helps catch problems early when ground support is far away. The prototype runs on simulated data, and can be connected to real wearable or on-board sensor data in future.
details:
What it does: AstroVitals tracks 13 daily health indicators (heart rate, HRV, blood pressure, sleep, exercise, mood, stress, reaction time, temperature, symptoms, weight, grip strength) plus radiation dose. It scores four health areas (Cardiovascular, Bone & Muscle, Immune, Behavioral) as Nominal, Watch or Alert, and gives clear recommended actions.

How it works: each astronaut is compared with their own first 21 days. Risk scores measure how far readings drift from that personal normal. An Isolation Forest model flags unusual combined patterns, and rules turn alerts into plain-language steps. Astronauts log a daily check-in, and can replay any mission day.

Benefits and impact: early warning and clearer decisions when contact with ground is delayed, supporting astronaut autonomy on missions to the Moon and Mars.

Tools: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, Streamlit, Matplotlib, GitHub. 13 automated tests check that the detector finds injected events and avoids false alarms.

Creativity: a personal-baseline approach instead of population averages, with explainable scores plus machine learning.

Factors considered: real astronaut data is restricted, so we used simulated data modeled on NASA's spaceflight hazards. Thresholds are illustrative, not medical advice.

Note: the Project Demonstration link downloads a 7-slide PDF.
